## Steps

### 1. Review Board State

Parse the pre-loaded board data above. Identify:
- All items with `status: backlog` or `status: current` (candidates for completion)
- Epics and their child tasks (via `parent` field)
- Blocked items and their blockers
- Items with terminal status (`done`, `processed`) that should be archived
- Items missing a required `status` field (all types except `reference`)

### 2. Gather Codebase Context

- Run `git log --oneline` for recent commits (last 30) to understand what work has been done
- Only Read full file bodies for tasks whose status is `backlog` or `current` AND whose title suggests overlap with recent commits
- Use the context budget escalation (Glob → Grep → Read with limit → Full read) for any additional lookups

### 3. Detect Completed Work

For each task with `status: backlog` or `status: current`, check if the work described has already been done:

- Look at recent commits for evidence the work was completed
- Check the codebase for the feature/fix the task describes
- If the work is done, flag it for status update to `done`

### 4. Detect New Work Needed

Scan for things that should become tasks but aren't tracked yet:

- Check recent commits for TODOs or FIXMEs introduced in code
- Look at open epics — are there obvious next steps not yet captured as tasks?
- Check if any `blocked_by` dependencies have been resolved (unblocking tasks)

### 5. Update Epic Progress

For each active epic:

- Check if all child tasks are `done` — if so, flag the epic as `done`
- Check if any child tasks are `current` — if so, the epic should be `current`
- Update the task list in the epic body if tasks have been added/removed

### 6. Check for Stale Items

- Tasks marked `current` but with no related commits in the last 30 days
- Epics in `planning` with no child tasks
- Resources stuck in `inbox` or `processing`

### 7. Present Changes

Present ALL proposed changes as a single summary before making any edits:

# Retrofit landing page dev flags to the shared convention

The landing page already uses `?dev=fallback` and `?dev=stale` query params (`landing/index.html:151-155`), but it predates the cross-project shared convention documented in REFE-0001. Retrofit to match.

## Gaps vs. REFE-0001

1. **No localStorage persistence.** Current implementation reads the URL param on each page load only. Per the spec, flags should persist to `dev-mode` / `dev-tools` keys so the param only needs to appear once per browser to "stick."
2. **No `?dev=off` clear semantics.** The spec defines `?dev=off` and `?dev=` as explicit clears. Currently there's no way to clear persisted state other than removing the param manually.
3. **No `?tools=` support.** Not used yet, but the module should expose it from the start so future overlays can use it without re-wiring.
4. **Inline script instead of shared module.** Current flag parsing lives inline in `landing/index.html`. Per REFE-0001, the reference implementation should be a shared vanilla-JS/TS module at `landing/src/lib/dev-flags.ts` that exposes `getDevMode()`, `getDevTools()`, `hasTool()`, and `syncDevFlagsFromUrl()`.

## Implementation

1. Create `landing/src/lib/dev-flags.ts` implementing the four exports from REFE-0001.
2. Gate persistence on `location.hostname === 'localhost'` — the current gating pattern (don't write localStorage in production).
3. Refactor `landing/index.html` to import the module and call `syncDevFlagsFromUrl()` at the top of the script block, then read via `getDevMode()` instead of the current inline `new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('dev')`.
4. Verify the existing `?dev=fallback` and `?dev=stale` still work identically, plus:
   - `?dev=off` clears the persisted mode
   - Navigating to a param-less URL preserves the persisted mode
   - `localStorage.setItem('dev-mode', 'stale')` also works (programmatic escape hatch)

## Local testing

- `http://localhost:8788/?dev=fallback` → fallback state visible
- Navigate to `http://localhost:8788/` (no param) → fallback state should PERSIST because it's in localStorage
- `http://localhost:8788/?dev=off` → clears, normal state returns
- Devtools: `localStorage.setItem('dev-mode', 'stale'); location.reload()` → stale state visible

## Acceptance

- `landing/src/lib/dev-flags.ts` exists and matches the REFE-0001 reference implementation shape
- Existing `?dev=fallback` / `?dev=stale` behavior preserved
- `?dev=off` clears persisted mode; bare `?dev=` also clears
- Persisted state survives navigation to a clean URL
- `localStorage` keys are `dev-mode` and `dev-tools` exactly
- REFE-0001 "Current modes" table for landing has the retrofit note removed

# Infrastructure and DevOps

Remove manual steps from the deploy workflow and add durable storage so the service doesn't depend on NASA's uptime for every cache miss.

## Priority focus: show today's image reliably

Recent incidents (video APOD tripping walkback, unexplained NASA API 500 on 2026-04-08) have repeatedly hurt the core promise — showing today's image reliably. TASK-0020 shipped alongside EPIC-0004's TASK-0019; TASK-0021 (cron warming) is the remaining P1.

## Tasks

### ~~TASK-0020: HTML scraping fallback for NASA API outages~~ [done]

Shipped with TASK-0019. `scrapeApodForDate` + `parseApodHtml` in `src/index.ts` kick in from `handleUpstreamFailure` whenever the API errors and stale cache is empty. Handles UTF-8 and UTF-16 LE/BE APOD pages (NASA silently serves some pages as UTF-16 LE with BOM despite a UTF-8 Content-Type header). **Directly addresses the 2026-04-08 outage.**

### TASK-0021: Automated daily cache warming via Cron Trigger [P1]

Add a `scheduled()` handler with a cron trigger to warm the edge cache after APOD rollover. Calls `findLatestImage`, `fetchImageCached`, and `fetchImageDimensions` to populate metadata and image bytes proactively. **Combined with TASK-0020, guarantees a fresh entry in stale cache so outages never exhaust our fallback.**

### TASK-0011: Add R2 storage layer for APOD image archiving

Insert R2 between edge cache and NASA as a persistent origin. Every image fetched from NASA gets stored in R2, building an automatic archive. Layered lookup becomes: Edge cache -> R2 -> NASA.

Key structure: `{date}/hd.{ext}`, `{date}/sd.{ext}`, `{date}/info.json`. Current-day images re-validated against NASA for same-day corrections; past dates served from R2 unconditionally.

R2 archiving also unblocks TASK-0031 Phase 2 (local timezone rollover, ahead-of-ET) and TASK-0035 (gallery/archive).

Blocked by TASK-0010.

### TASK-0032: GitHub Action auto-deploy on merge to main

Workflow triggered on push to `main`. Runs type-check (`npx tsc --noEmit`) as a gate, then `npm run deploy`. Requires `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` as repository secrets. Spawned from NOTE-0014.

## Sequence

1. ~~TASK-0020~~ — done
2. **TASK-0021** [P1] — Cron cache warming. Now that scrape is in place, cron warming guarantees stale cache never runs dry.
3. TASK-0011 — R2 storage layer. Larger effort, unblocks follow-on features (gallery, timezone Phase 2).
4. TASK-0032 — GitHub Action. Small, can be done anytime.

## Cross-EPIC Dependencies

- EPIC-0002 TASK-0031 Phase 2 (local timezone, ahead-of-ET) is blocked by TASK-0011
- EPIC-0006-worth gallery/archive work (TASK-0035) is blocked by TASK-0011

# Landing page bug cleanup

Residual bugs from NOTE-0017 that are small enough to batch into a single cleanup pass. (Several other items from the original critique have already been resolved by subsequent landing work.)

## Items

### 1. `--font-weight-medmium` typo in `_hero.scss`
`landing/src/styles/_hero.scss:43` has `font-weight: var(--font-weight-medmium)` (typo: "medmium"). The variable defined in `_variables.scss:20` is the correctly-spelled `--font-weight-medium`. The typo'd reference resolves to nothing, so the rule silently does nothing.

**Fix**: change `_hero.scss:43` from `var(--font-weight-medmium)` to `var(--font-weight-medium)`. No edit to `_variables.scss` needed — the variable name there is already correct.

### 2. Endpoint list missing `/optimized` and `/thumb`
`landing/index.html` endpoint list (around line 87) shows only `/`, `/sd`, `/info`, `/about`. `/optimized` and `/thumb` are valid routes and should be documented alongside the others. Keep `/` prominent as the primary use case.

### 3. Verify caption spread on wide viewports
NOTE-0017 flagged that title and date spread across the full image width on desktop, feeling scattered rather than intimate. Verify against the current layout and tighten if still an issue (constrain caption width or cluster elements under the image edge). Close as verified-fixed if no longer applicable.

## Acceptance

- Typo fixed; rule resolves to the intended weight (visually verified)
- Endpoint list includes `/optimized` and `/thumb` with descriptions consistent with existing rows
- Caption layout feels intimate on wide viewports, or explicitly verified as already resolved

The focus toggle now has visible "Focus" text alongside the icon, but the markup was not updated when the label was added. Spawned from NOTE-0017 (remaining items).

## Problems

- **Accessible-name mismatch.** `index.html:131` has `aria-label="Dim the lights"` but the visible `<span class="label">` says "Focus". When a button has visible text, `aria-label` overrides what screen readers announce, so sighted users see "Focus" while screen reader users hear "Dim the lights". WCAG 2.5.3 (Label in Name) failure.
- **No toggle semantics.** This is a binary on/off toggle but has no `aria-pressed` state. Assistive tech can't tell whether focus mode is active.
- **Redundant `title` tooltip.** Now that text is visible, the `title="Dim the lights"` attribute is noise (and also stale).
- **Tiny label size.** `.label` is `font-size: 0.5rem` (~8px) at `_focus-mode.scss:29`, smaller than ideal for discoverability.

## Fix

- Remove `aria-label` (let the visible "Focus" text be the accessible name), or update it to match the visible text
- Remove the `title` attribute
- Add `aria-pressed` reflecting focus-mode state, updated in the click handler when `.focus-mode` is toggled on `body`
- Bump `.label` font-size so it reads clearly without squinting (tune alongside icon for balance)

## Acceptance

- Accessible name matches visible text (no mismatch flagged by axe / Lighthouse)
- `aria-pressed="true"` when focus mode is active, `"false"` otherwise
- Label is readable at default zoom without squinting
- Existing focus-mode behavior (overlay, Esc, overlay click to exit) is unchanged

# Video APOD Resilience

Make the service handle video APODs and upstream failures gracefully, so image endpoints never 500 when a working fallback exists, and never show days-old content when a same-day thumbnail is available.

See NOTE-0026 for full context and discovery.

## Status: done

Both reliability goals are shipped. Video days with a NASA-provided `thumbnail_url` now serve the thumbnail directly (no stale walkback), and upstream API outages now fall through to an HTML scrape of `apod.nasa.gov/apod/` before giving up. The two changes landed together because they share the same plumbing: `resolveApod()`, `findLatestResolvable()`, and `handleUpstreamFailure()` all live in `src/index.ts`.

## Tasks

- ~~TASK-0018~~ — walkback error handling (shipped `997371e`)
- ~~TASK-0019~~ — video APOD thumbnail support
- ~~TASK-0020~~ — HTML scrape fallback (cross-filed under EPIC-0003 but closed as part of the same shipment)

## Cross-EPIC Dependencies

- EPIC-0003 TASK-0011 (R2 storage) would add an archival layer on top of this, but is not required — the scrape + thumbnail path already closes the two reliability holes that motivated this epic.

# Social Sharing Previews

Make link previews render correctly on Twitter, Slack, Facebook, Discord, iMessage, and friends. Covers both the HTML surface (so crawlers see OG tags instead of image bytes) and the image asset itself (so the preview is sized and cropped for social platforms).

## Tasks

### TASK-0034: Serve OG HTML to social crawlers

Sniff `User-Agent` on image routes. Return HTML with OG + Twitter-card tags for known crawlers, unchanged image bytes for everyone else. Skips the upstream image fetch entirely on the crawler path.

### TASK-0033: Generate daily OG image via workers-og

Render a 1200x630 branded PNG once per day inside the Worker via Satori. Cached 24h keyed to date, regenerates at rollover. The OG HTML then points `og:image` at `/og` instead of `/sd`.

## Sequence

1. **TASK-0034 first** (OG HTML) — immediately fixes preview rendering even using the raw image URL for `og:image`
2. **TASK-0033 second** (OG image) — upgrades preview quality to a properly sized and branded card

## Related

- NOTE-0020 (OG HTML for crawlers) — spawning note for TASK-0034
- NOTE-0008 (OG image generation) — spawning note for TASK-0033
- TASK-0022 (annotated image endpoint) — shares the rendering pipeline with TASK-0033, candidate for refactor after both land

## Validation Rules

### Status Transitions

Validate transitions using the script:

```bash
bash "/Users/grant/Documents/Projects/BoardPM/plugin/scripts/validate-status.sh" <type> <from_status> <to_status>
```

Exit codes: `0` = valid forward transition, `2` = backward transition (confirm with user), `1` = invalid.

Valid forward transitions:

| Type | Valid Transitions |
|------|-------------------|
| task | `backlog` → `current` → `done` |
| epic | `planning` → `current` → `done` |
| resource | `inbox` → `processing` → `processed` |
| note | `inbox` → `processed` |
| adr | `active` → `superseded` or `active` → `deprecated` |

Backward transitions (e.g., `done` → `backlog`) are allowed but should confirm with the user first — they may indicate a reopened task.

### ADR Immutability

ADRs are **immutable**. The only permitted edit is changing `status` (to `superseded` or `deprecated`). If the user asks to edit ADR content, explain that ADRs are write-once and suggest:
- Adding a dated addendum at the bottom of the file
- Creating a new ADR that supersedes the old one (via `/board:board-add adr`)

If setting an ADR to `superseded`, ask for the superseding ADR ID and add `superseded_by` to the frontmatter.

### Task Title Changes

If editing a task title (the `# heading` or filename), enforce imperative mood. If the new title is a noun phrase, rewrite it (e.g., "authentication" → "Add authentication").

Renaming also requires renaming the file to match: `TASK-NNNN_new-kebab-case-title.md`. Use `git mv` to preserve history.

### Reference Docs

REFE items have no status field. Edits to reference content are unrestricted — they are meant to be kept current.

### Priority Values

Only `1` (high), `2` (medium), or `3` (low) are valid. Reject other values.

## Editable Fields

| Field | Types | Notes |
|-------|-------|-------|
| `status` | all except reference | Must follow valid transitions |
| `priority` | task | Values: 1, 2, 3 |
| `blocked_by` | task | List of task IDs; add or remove individual blockers |
| `parent` | task | Link to parent epic |
| `due` | task | Date value |
| `tags` | all | List of strings; add or remove individual tags |
| `title` | all | Rename heading + file; imperative mood for tasks |
| `body` | all except adr | Freeform content below frontmatter |
| `superseded_by` | adr | Only when setting status to superseded |
| `url` | resource | Primary external URL |
| `type` | all except adr | Retype/convert — creates new file, deletes old (see below) |

## Retype (Convert Type)

When the user asks to convert or retype an item (e.g., "convert TASK-0022 to a note", "retype this as an epic"):

### Validation

1. **Refuse if source is ADR** — ADRs are immutable. Explain why and suggest creating a new item separately.
2. **Confirm with user** — "This will delete TASK-0022 and create a new NOTE with the next available ID. Proceed?"

### Procedure

1. **Get next ID** for the target type:
   ```bash
   bash "/Users/grant/Documents/Projects/BoardPM/plugin/scripts/next-id.sh" <TARGET_TYPE> ./board
   ```
2. **Create new file** with:
   - Correct type prefix and ID in filename
   - Correct directory for the target type
   - Correct frontmatter (initial status for new type, carry over applicable fields)
   - Body content carried over from old item
   - Title adjusted if needed (e.g., imperative mood for TASKs, relaxed for NOTEs)
3. **Delete old file** via `git rm`
4. **Find and update cross-references** — use Grep to search for the old ID across all board files:
   - `blocked_by` lists
   - `parent` fields
   - `tasks` lists (in EPICs)
   - `spawned` lists (in NOTEs)
   - Wiki-links (`[[OLD-ID]]`) in body content

   Update each reference to the new ID.
5. **Report** the change: `Retyped: TASK-0022 → NOTE-0005 (old file deleted, references updated)`

### Type-Specific Adjustments

| Target Type | Adjustments |
|-------------|-------------|
| task | Title must be imperative mood; `status: backlog`; add `priority: 2` |
| epic | Title stays imperative; `status: planning`; consider adding `tasks:` list |
| note | `status: inbox`; title can relax imperative mood |
| reference | No status field; content must be objective/encyclopedic |
| resource | Requires `url` (ask user); `status: inbox` |

## Execution

1. Apply the edit via targeted frontmatter field replacement (use Edit tool, not full file rewrite)
2. If renaming, use `git mv` for the file and update the `# heading`
3. **If the status change results in a terminal status** (`done` for tasks/epics, `processed` for resources/notes), archive the item immediately after updating the status:
   ```bash
   bash "/Users/grant/Documents/Projects/BoardPM/plugin/scripts/archive-batch.sh" ./board <file_path>
   ```
   ADRs are the sole exception — they are never archived regardless of status.
   If the user explicitly asks NOT to archive, respect that but note the lint warning they will see.
4. Show a summary of what changed: `TASK-0003: status backlog → done → archived`
5. If the edit unblocks other tasks (a blocker was marked `done`), mention which tasks are now unblocked

## Notes

- **Avoid redundant invocations** — if this skill was already invoked earlier in the session and the board has not been modified since, reuse the previous board data instead of invoking again

## Steps

### 1. Lint Results

The following lint output is pre-loaded (checks: frontmatter validity, required fields, status/priority values, directory placement, filename patterns, duplicate IDs, ADRs in archive, broken references):

!`bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/board-lint.sh" ./board 2>&1`

### 2. Interpret Results

Parse the lint output above. Each line is either:
- `ERROR: <file>: <message>` — must be fixed
- `WARN:  <file>: <message>` — should be reviewed

If no issues found, report that the board is healthy and stop.

### 3. Present Issues

Group issues by file and present them clearly:

```
## Board Health Report

### Errors (must fix)
- TASK-0003_add-caching.md: Invalid status 'wip' (must be backlog|current|done)
- ADR-0001_chose-redis.md: ADR is in archive/ — must move back to planning/

### Warnings (review)
- RESO-0002_redis-article.md: Missing field: url
```

### 4. Offer Fixes

For each error, offer to fix it:

- **Invalid status**: Ask the user what the correct status should be, then use `/board:board-edit` to update
- **Wrong directory**: Offer to move the file to the correct directory via `git mv`
- **Missing fields**: Ask the user for the value, then add it to frontmatter
- **Duplicate IDs**: Offer to reassign one of the duplicates using `next-id.sh`
- **ADR in archive**: Offer to move it back to `board/planning/`
- **Broken references**: Ask if the reference should be removed or if a missing file should be created

### 5. LLM-Only Checks

After script-based validation, perform checks that require language understanding:

- **Task title mood**: Scan task files and check if titles use imperative mood (verb-first). Flag noun phrases like "User Authentication" that should be "Add user authentication".
- **ADR completeness**: Check if ADRs have a "Spawned Items" section. If missing, flag it.

Present these as suggestions, not errors — they require judgment.

### 6. Re-validate

After fixing issues, run the lint script again to confirm all errors are resolved.
````

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# board-lint.sh — Validate all board files for structural and data issues.
# Usage: board-lint.sh [--hook|--no-fail] [board_root]
#   board_root defaults to ./board
#   --hook / --no-fail: always exit 0, and stay silent when the board is clean or
#                       there is no board/ directory (for SessionStart hook use)
#
# Compatible with bash 3.2+ (macOS default).
#
# Exit codes:
#   0 — no issues (or no board/ directory found, or --hook mode)
#   1 — errors found (strict mode only)
#
# Output:
#   stdout — summary lines ("Board lint: ...")
#   stderr — per-file ERROR/WARN findings

set -euo pipefail

NO_FAIL=0
BOARD_ROOT=""
for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
        --hook|--no-fail) NO_FAIL=1 ;;
        -*) echo "Unknown flag: $arg" >&2; exit 2 ;;
        *)  BOARD_ROOT="$arg" ;;
    esac
done
BOARD_ROOT="${BOARD_ROOT:-./board}"

fi

# Validate cross-references
validate_references

# --- Summary ---

if [[ $errors -eq 0 && $warnings -eq 0 ]]; then
    [[ $NO_FAIL -eq 1 ]] || echo "Board lint: all files valid."
    exit 0
elif [[ $errors -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "Board lint: $warnings warning(s), 0 errors."
    exit 0
elif [[ $NO_FAIL -eq 1 ]]; then
    # Findings went to stderr, which the session hook does not surface — point at the skill
    echo "Board lint: $errors error(s), $warnings warning(s) — run /board:board-lint to review."
    exit 0
else
    echo "Board lint: $errors error(s), $warnings warning(s)."
    exit 1
fi

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-21 01:42:16Z)**_

Yes, there's a real bug, and the BoardPM board doesn't track it yet.

**The bug:** `skills/board-lint/SKILL.md:17` pre-loads its data with this line:

```
!`bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/board-lint.sh" ./board 2>&1`
```

Without a flag, `board-lint.sh` runs in strict mode and exits 1 whenever it finds errors (`scripts/board-lint.sh:444`). Claude Code treats a non-zero exit in a `!` injection as a failure and refuses to load the skill. So the skill only loads when the board has no errors, which is when it isn't needed. The SessionStart hook still says "run /board:board-lint to review", and that path always fails.

**Fix (one line):**

```
!`bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/board-lint.sh" ./board 2>&1 || true`
```

Use `|| true` rather than `--no-fail`. `--no-fail` also suppresses the "all files valid." line when the board is clean. The skill would then get empty output and couldn't reliably tell the user the board is healthy.

None of the other skills have this problem. They pre-load with `board-scan.sh`/`board-show.sh`, which only exit non-zero on real failures.

Suggested task title for the BoardPM repo: **"Fix board-lint skill failing to load when lint finds errors"**. It's small enough that you could just make the one-line edit instead of filing it.

# Board Lint

Validate board files for structural and data issues, and help fix any problems found. The system spec is bundled with the plugin at `/Users/grant/Documents/Projects/BoardPM/plugin/spec/board-system-spec.md`.

## Steps

### 1. Lint Results

The following lint output is pre-loaded (checks: frontmatter validity, required fields, status/priority values, directory placement, filename patterns, duplicate IDs, ADRs in archive, broken references):

Board lint: all files valid.

### 2. Interpret Results

Parse the lint output above. Each line is either:
- `ERROR: <file>: <message>` — must be fixed
- `WARN:  <file>: <message>` — should be reviewed

If no issues found, report that the board is healthy and stop.

### 3. Present Issues

Group issues by file and present them clearly:

```
## Board Health Report

### Errors (must fix)
- TASK-0003_add-caching.md: Invalid status 'wip' (must be backlog|current|done)
- ADR-0001_chose-redis.md: ADR is in archive/ — must move back to planning/

### Warnings (review)
- RESO-0002_redis-article.md: Missing field: url
```

### 4. Offer Fixes

For each error, offer to fix it:

- **Invalid status**: Ask the user what the correct status should be, then use `/board:board-edit` to update
- **Wrong directory**: Offer to move the file to the correct directory via `git mv`
- **Missing fields**: Ask the user for the value, then add it to frontmatter
- **Duplicate IDs**: Offer to reassign one of the duplicates using `next-id.sh`
- **ADR in archive**: Offer to move it back to `board/planning/`
- **Broken references**: Ask if the reference should be removed or if a missing file should be created

### 5. LLM-Only Checks

After script-based validation, perform checks that require language understanding:

- **Task title mood**: Scan task files and check if titles use imperative mood (verb-first). Flag noun phrases like "User Authentication" that should be "Add user authentication".
- **ADR completeness**: Check if ADRs have a "Spawned Items" section. If missing, flag it.

Present these as suggestions, not errors — they require judgment.

### 6. Re-validate

After fixing issues, run the lint script again to confirm all errors are resolved.

**1. The skill won't load when the board has lint errors (the main one).**
Line 17 runs `board-lint.sh ./board` to pre-load the results. Without a flag, the script exits 1 whenever it finds errors (`scripts/board-lint.sh:444`). Claude Code treats a non-zero exit in a `!` injection as a failure and refuses to load the skill. Today the SessionStart hook reported 29 errors and told you to run `/board:board-lint`, and that run failed with `Shell command failed for pattern...`. !`bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/board-lint.sh" ./board 2>&1 || true`

Step 2 says "If no issues found, report that the board is healthy and stop." So step 5 (title mood, ADR completeness) is skipped on a clean board. Combined with bug 1, step 5 never runs: the skill only loads on a clean board, and on a clean board it stops at step 2.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-21 01:45:39Z)**_

Here's the task, ready to hand to `/board:board-add` in the BoardPM repo:

````markdown
# Run LLM-only checks in board-lint when the script reports no issues

priority: 3
related: the companion task that adds `|| true` to the board-lint pre-load (separate bug)

## Problem

In `plugin/skills/board-lint/SKILL.md`, step 2 ends with:

> If no issues found, report that the board is healthy and stop. (line 25)

That early exit comes before step 5 (LLM-Only Checks, lines 53-60). Step 5 runs the checks the shell script can't:

- **Task title mood:** flags noun-phrase task titles. The spec requires imperative mood (`spec/board-system-spec.md:473`).
- **ADR completeness:** flags ADRs that have no "Spawned Items" section (`spec/board-system-spec.md:213`).

`board-lint.sh` doesn't check either of these. So a board with no ERROR or WARN lines never gets a title-mood or ADR-completeness review. The skill reports "healthy" while spec violations remain.

## Evidence

In nasa-picture-proxy on 2026-10-20, `/board:board-lint` reported `Board lint: all files valid.` and stopped. The board still had four active tasks with non-imperative titles:

- TASK-0021 "Automated daily cache warming via Cron Trigger"
- TASK-0022 "Annotated image endpoint with title and explanation"
- TASK-0030 "Landing page bug cleanup"
- TASK-0031 "Local timezone APOD rollover"

## Interaction with the pre-load bug

The line 17 pre-load (`board-lint.sh ./board 2>&1`) exits 1 when it finds errors, and Claude Code then refuses to load the skill. So until that is fixed, the skill only loads on a board with no errors, and this early exit then fires every time. Together the two bugs mean step 5 never runs. Fixing either one alone still leaves step 5 skipped in one of the two cases.

## Fix

1. Change line 25 to:
   > If no issues found, report that structural checks pass, then skip to step 5.
2. Add a line at the top of step 5:
   > Always run this step, even when the script reported no issues.
3. Limit step 5's title-mood scan to active tasks (`board/tasks/`), not `board/archive/`. Once step 5 runs on every invocation, archived titles would otherwise be flagged every time. Renaming archived files only adds history noise.
4. Leave step 6 (Re-validate) as it is. It already says "After fixing issues", so a clean board skips it naturally.

## Acceptance

- On a board where the script reports `all files valid.`, the skill still reports title-mood and ADR-completeness suggestions.
- On a board with script errors, step 5 still runs after steps 3-4. This only works once the pre-load fix lands.
- Archived tasks are not flagged for title mood.
- The step 5 results are still presented as suggestions, not errors.
````

 ## Commands
 
-```bash
-npm run dev            # Start API (localhost:8787) + landing (localhost:8788) in background

-npm run dev:landing    # Landing page Vite dev server only

-npm run log:api        # Tail API logs only

+- `npm run dev` starts the API (localhost:8787) and landing page (localhost:8788) in the background. Check them with `npm run status`, stop them with `npm run stop`, and read logs with the `npm run log:*` scripts.
+- Type-check with `npx tsc --noEmit`. There is no build artifact; Wrangler bundles `src/` directly.
 
 ## Architecture
 
-Single-file Worker (`src/index.ts`) with these routes (plus `.jpg` aliases for each image endpoint):
-
-- `GET /` — proxies today's HD APOD image (falls back to standard if unavailable)
-- `GET /sd` — proxies the standard-res version
-- `GET /optimized` — optimized image (≤1200px, auto WebP/AVIF via Cloudflare Image Transformations)
-- `GET /thumb` — tiny blurred thumbnail (32px WebP, ~1KB via Cloudflare Image Transformations)
-- `GET /info` — returns JSON metadata (includes image width/height)
-- `GET /about` — plain-text description and attribution
-
 Caching uses the Workers Cache API (`caches.default`) with a two-tier strategy — no KV, D1, or cron:
 - **Primary cache** (6h TTL): APOD metadata keyed by ET date, image bytes keyed by NASA URL
 - **Stale fallback** (24h TTL): same data under a `:stale` suffixed key, served when NASA's API is down or rate-limited
 
 Cache keys are date-based in `America/New_York` timezone, so they roll over at midnight ET. Cache key URLs must use a zone-scoped hostname (`https://api.nasapicture.com/_cache/...`), not synthetic hostnames -- `caches.default` silently drops writes for unknown hosts.
 
-Concurrent requests for the same APOD date are coalesced via an in-flight promise map to avoid thundering herd on cold cache.
-
-The `findLatestImage` function walks backwards from today up to `MAX_LOOKBACK_DAYS` (7) to skip video APODs.
-
-The landing page (`landing/`) is built with Vite and SCSS, served at `nasapicture.com` via Cloudflare Pages. Source is `landing/index.html` with styles in `landing/src/styles/` (SCSS partials). The landing page fetches `/info` and `/thumb` in parallel to pre-size the image container and show a blurred placeholder while the full image loads. -
-### Users
-Everyone — developers integrating the API into dashboards and side projects, tinkerers building for fun, and general visitors who stumble on the domain out of curiosity about space. The landing page should be immediately understandable to non-technical visitors while giving developers everything they need.
-
-### Brand Personality
-**Clever, minimal, precise.** The voice is confident and concise — says a lot with few words. Engineering craft without jargon. Personality comes through in small details (the /about ASCII art, "That's it. That's the whole integration."), never through excess.
-
-### Emotional Goals
-**Awe + simplicity.** Visitors should feel wonder at the cosmos (the APOD image does the heavy lifting) and relief at how easy the tool is. The design should get out of the way of the content while still feeling crafted.
-
-### Aesthetic Direction
-- **Theme**: Dark space — deep void (#05070c) with atmospheric depth, not flat black
-- **Accent**: Warm amber/gold (#e8a838) — planned but not yet implemented; current palette is monochrome silver with NASA blue
-- **Typography**: Source Serif 4 Display (headings), Source Sans 3 (body), Source Code Pro (code) — Adobe Typekit, no generic fonts
-- **Layout**: Generous whitespace, content-forward, max-width constrained (~5xl)
-- **Motion**: Subtle and purposeful — twinkling stars, staggered fade-ins, gentle hover lifts. Always respect `prefers-reduced-motion`
-- **Anti-references**: No AI slop aesthetics, no purple gradients on white, no cookie-cutter SaaS layouts
-
-### Design Principles
-1. **The image is the hero** — everything else supports it. Never compete with the APOD for attention.
-2. **Earn trust through restraint** — fewer elements, better. If it doesn't serve the visitor, remove it.
-3. **Craft in the details** — personality lives in small moments (ASCII art, code comments, hover states), not in loud design choices.
-4. **Accessible by default** — WCAG AA contrast, semantic HTML, reduced-motion alternatives. Accessibility is not optional.
-5. **Zero friction** — the landing page mirrors the API philosophy: simple to deploy, simple to understand.
-

## Check 3 — trim derivable content from checked-in CLAUDE.md files

A line of a checked-in CLAUDE.md that a fresh session could reconstruct with a few tool calls (`ls`, `cat`, reading the manifest, `--help`) is dead weight every session it loads into pays for. Scan each checked-in CLAUDE.md file — the root file and `.claude/CLAUDE.md` (always loaded), nested-directory CLAUDE.md files (loaded when working under that directory), and `.claude/rules/*.md` — for content that is derivable from the codebase and propose deleting it outright. Always-loaded files matter most; nested files still get scanned. LOCAL files (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`) are check 2's domain; leave them alone here.

The derivability test, per section: could a session working in this repo reconstruct this by reading the code? If yes, cut it. If no, keep it.

- **Cut — derivable from the codebase**: directory and file layouts (what `ls`/`find` already show); tech-stack and dependency lists (what the package manifest — `package.json`, `Cargo.toml`, `pyproject.toml`, `go.mod` — already says); build/test/lint commands that are the standard invocation for the tool or are listed in the manifest's scripts; API signatures, type definitions, and schemas copied from source; architecture overviews and repo tours that read like a README (the codebase is the README); generic best practices the model already follows ("write clean code", "handle errors properly", "add tests"); and rules a pre-commit hook, lint config, or CI check already enforces mechanically — cross-check candidates against `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and the lint/format configs before keeping them.
- **Keep — not derivable from the codebase**: gotchas and failure contracts ("X looks safe but does Y"); design rationale and "why it's this way" that the code can't explain; non-standard conventions that DIFFER from language or tool defaults (so the code alone would teach the wrong pattern); agent directives and safety-critical prohibitions ("never push to main", "never edit generated/"); repo etiquette (branch naming, PR conventions, commit style); domain glossaries; build/test commands that are NOT guessable (non-standard scripts, required flags, environment setup); and pointers to context that lives elsewhere (`@path/to/import` lines, skill references).
- **When unsure, keep it.** The user wrote these files; a borderline line stays. Never cut a "never do X" rule on the grounds that it looks generic — safety-critical prohibitions are keep-always, same as check 4.

Prioritize files at or near the large-CLAUDE.md warning threshold — Claude Code warns when a single loaded memory file exceeds roughly 5% of the model's context window in characters, with a floor of ~40,000 chars (`getMaxMemoryCharacterCount` in `src/utils/claudemd.ts` in the Claude Code repo) — and state in the report which files trip it before vs after the proposed cuts. Files under the threshold with substantial derivable content still get a trim proposal; files that are already lean get one line ("already lean — nothing to cut") and no proposal.

Propose per file: the categories being cut with approximate line counts ("directory layout — 31 lines", "tech stack — 8 lines"), the est. resident tokens saved, and what remains. Quote each removed block verbatim in the proposal so the user can judge and so the edit is reversible from the report. This check runs BEFORE check 4's migration so that migration operates on the kept content only — don't propose migrating anything this check proposes to delete.

All of that is derived from the history files, so tracking it only adds churn to every commit and causes merge conflicts if you work from more than one machine.

I committed it in `8bdbb23` by mistake. To fix that:

```
echo '.specstory/statistics.json' >> .gitignore
git rm --cached .specstory/statistics.json
```

Keep `.specstory/.project.json` and `cli/config.toml` tracked, since those are project config.

Should I apply this and commit it as `chore(specstory): untrack statistics.json`?

### Brand Personality
**Clever, minimal, precise.** The voice is confident and concise — says a lot with few words. Engineering craft without jargon. Personality comes through in small details (the /about ASCII art, "That's it. That's the whole integration."), never through excess.

### Emotional Goals
**Awe + simplicity.** Visitors should feel wonder at the cosmos (the APOD image does the heavy lifting) and relief at how easy the tool is. The design should get out of the way of the content while still feeling crafted.

196	  const inflight = inflightApod.get(cacheKey);
197	  if (inflight) {
198	    log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${cacheKey} → coalesced with in-flight request`);
199	    return inflight;
200	  }
201	
202	  const promise = fetchApodFromNasa(log, devFlags, apiKey, resolvedDate, cacheKey, cacheReq, staleReq);
203	  inflightApod.set(cacheKey, promise);
204	  try {
205	    return await promise;
206	  } finally {
207	    inflightApod.delete(cacheKey);
208	  }
209	}
210	
211	async function handleUpstreamFailure(
212	  log: string[],
213	  cache: Cache,
214	  cacheReq: Request,
215	  staleReq: Request,
216	  resolvedDate: string,
217	  cacheKey: string,
218	  upstreamStatus: number,
219	): Promise<ApodResponse> {
220	  // Stale cache is the first, cheapest fallback.
221	  const stale = await cache.match(staleReq);
222	  if (stale) {
223	    log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${cacheKey} → stale cache fallback`);
224	    return stale.json() as Promise<ApodResponse>;
225	  }
226	
227	  // Last resort: scrape the APOD webpage. It has historically stayed up
228	  // when the JSON API returns 5xx.
229	  try {
230	    const scraped = await scrapeApodForDate(log, resolvedDate);
231	    log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${cacheKey} → scrape fallback activated (source: apod.nasa.gov webpage)`);
232	    await writeApodCaches(cache, cacheReq, staleReq, scraped);
233	    return scraped;
234	  } catch (scrapeErr) {
235	    const msg = scrapeErr instanceof Error ? scrapeErr.message : "unknown";
236	    log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${cacheKey} → scrape failed: ${msg}`);
237	  }
238	
239	  throw new NasaApiError(
240	    upstreamStatus,
241	    upstreamStatus === 429
242	      ? "NASA API rate limit exceeded — try again later"
243	      : `NASA API returned ${upstreamStatus}`,
244	  );
245	}
246	
247	async function fetchApodFromNasa(
248	  log: string[], devFlags: DevFlags, apiKey: string, resolvedDate: string, cacheKey: string,
249	  cacheReq: Request, staleReq: Request,
250	): Promise<ApodResponse> {
251	  const cache = caches.default;
252	
253	  if (devFlags.enabled && devFlags.mode === "nasa-error") {
254	    log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${cacheKey} → dev simulated nasa-error (skipping upstream)`);
255	    return handleUpstreamFailure(log, cache, cacheReq, staleReq, resolvedDate, cacheKey, 500);
256	  }
257	
258	  const url = `${NASA_APOD_URL}?api_key=${apiKey}&date=${resolvedDate}`;
259	  const res = await fetch(url);
260	
261	  const cfCache = res.headers.get("cf-cache-status") ?? "none";
262	  log.push(`  [fetchApod] ${cacheKey} → ${res.status} (cf-cache: ${cfCache})`);
263	
264	  if (!res.ok) {
265	    const body = await res.text();
266	    log.push(`  [fetchApod] body=${body}`);
267	    return handleUpstreamFailure(log, cache, cacheReq, staleReq, resolvedDate, cacheKey, res.status);
268	  }
269	
270	  const apod = await res.json() as ApodResponse;
271	  await writeApodCaches(cache, cacheReq, staleReq, apod);
272	  return apod;
273	}
274	
275	// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
276	// HTML scrape fallback — last-resort data source when NASA's JSON API
277	// fails and the stale cache is empty. The apod.nasa.gov/apod/ pages use a
278	// stable 1990s-era HTML layout, so regex extraction is reliable enough for
279	// a rescue path. See NOTE-0022 for the layout reverse-engineering.
280	// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
281	
282	const MONTH_NAMES = [
283	  "january", "february", "march", "april", "may", "june",
284	  "july", "august", "september", "october", "november", "december",
285	];
286	
287	function pageUrlForDate(date: string): string {
288	  // YYYY-MM-DD → apod.nasa.gov/apod/apYYMMDD.html
289	  const [yyyy, mm, dd] = date.split("-");
290	  return `${APOD_PAGE_BASE}ap${yyyy.slice(2)}${mm}${dd}.html`;
291	}
292	
293	function stripHtml(s: string): string {
294	  return s
295	    .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, " ")
296	    .replace(/&nbsp;/gi, " ")
297	    .replace(/&amp;/gi, "&")
298	    .replace(/&quot;/gi, '"')
299	    .replace(/&#39;/gi, "'")
300	    .replace(/&lt;/gi, "<")
301	    .replace(/&gt;/gi, ">")
302	    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
303	    .trim();
304	}
305	
306	async function scrapeApodForDate(log: string[], date: string): Promise<ApodResponse> {
307	  const pageUrl = pageUrlForDate(date);
308	  log.push(`  [scrape] GET ${pageUrl}`);
309	
310	  const res = await fetch(pageUrl, {
311	    headers: { "User-Agent": "nasa-picture-proxy/1.0 (+https://nasapicture.com)" },
312	  });
313	  if (!res.ok) {
314	    throw new Error(`scrape: ${pageUrl} returned ${res.status}`);
315	  }
316	
317	  // NASA's server declares Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8, but at least
318	  // some pages (observed: ap260408.html) are actually encoded as UTF-16 LE with
319	  // a BOM. Detect BOM and pick the right decoder ourselves rather than trust
320	  // the header.
321	  const buf = await res.arrayBuffer();
322	  const bytes = new Uint8Array(buf);
323	  let encoding = "utf-8";
324	  if (bytes.length >= 2 && bytes[0] === 0xff && bytes[1] === 0xfe) {
325	    encoding = "utf-16le";
326	  } else if (bytes.length >= 2 && bytes[0] === 0xfe && bytes[1] === 0xff) {
327	    encoding = "utf-16be";
328	  }
329	  const html = new TextDecoder(encoding).decode(bytes);
330	  log.push(`  [scrape] decoded ${bytes.length}B as ${encoding}`);
331	  return parseApodHtml(html, date);
332	}
333	
334	export function parseApodHtml(html: string, date: string): ApodResponse {
335	  // Video detection: APOD video days use an <iframe> instead of <img>.
336	  const hasIframe = /<iframe[\s>]/i.test(html);
337	  const mediaType: "image" | "video" = hasIframe ? "video" : "image";
338	
339	  // Title and date: both live in the <title> tag as "APOD: YYYY Month D  Title"
340	  // (older pages) or "APOD: YYYY Month D – Title" (newer pages introduce an
341	  // en-dash separator). Strip any leading en-dash/em-dash/hyphen from the
342	  // remainder so the title doesn't carry the separator.
343	  let title = "Astronomy Picture of the Day";
344	  let pageDate = date;
345	  const titleTag = html.match(/<title>\s*APOD:\s*([\s\S]*?)<\/title>/i);
346	  if (titleTag) {
347	    const inner = titleTag[1].replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
348	    const m = inner.match(/^(\d{4})\s+([A-Za-z]+)\s+(\d{1,2})\s+(.+)$/);
349	    if (m) {
350	      const [, y, monthName, d, rest] = m;
351	      const monthIdx = MONTH_NAMES.indexOf(monthName.toLowerCase());
352	      if (monthIdx >= 0) {
353	        const mm = String(monthIdx + 1).padStart(2, "0");
354	        const dd = String(Number(d)).padStart(2, "0");
355	        pageDate = `${y}-${mm}-${dd}`;
356	      }
357	      title = rest.replace(/^[\u2013\u2014-]\s*/, "").trim();
358	    }
359	  }
360	
361	  // Image URLs: the main photo sits inside <a href="image/…"><img src="image/…">.
362	  // The anchor points at the full-res file, the img at the display (SD) file.
363	  let url = "";
364	  let hdurl: string | undefined;
365	  const imgAnchor = html.match(
366	    /<a\s+href="(image\/[^"]+)"\s*>\s*<img\s+src="(image\/[^"]+)"/i,
367	  );
368	  if (imgAnchor) {
369	    hdurl = `${APOD_PAGE_BASE}${imgAnchor[1]}`;
370	    url = `${APOD_PAGE_BASE}${imgAnchor[2]}`;
371	  } else {
372	    const imgOnly = html.match(/<img\s+src="(image\/[^"]+)"/i);
373	    if (imgOnly) url = `${APOD_PAGE_BASE}${imgOnly[1]}`;
374	  }
375	
376	  // Explanation: text following "<b>Explanation:</b>" until the next <p> or <hr>.
377	  let explanation = "";
378	  const expMatch = html.match(
379	    /<b>\s*Explanation:\s*<\/b>([\s\S]*?)(?=<p>\s*<center>|<hr|<\/body>)/i,
380	  );
381	  if (expMatch) explanation = stripHtml(expMatch[1]);
382	
383	  // Credit/copyright: labelled "Image Credit:" or "Credit & Copyright:". Capture
384	  // text through end of the nearest <p>/<center>/<hr> block.
385	  let copyright: string | undefined;
386	  const creditMatch = html.match(
387	    /<b>\s*(?:Image Credit(?:\s*(?:&amp;|&)\s*Copyright)?|Credit(?:\s*(?:&amp;|&)\s*Copyright)?)\s*:\s*<\/b>([\s\S]*?)(?=<\/p>|<\/center>|<hr|<b>\s*Explanation)/i,
388	  );
389	  if (creditMatch) {
390	    const credit = stripHtml(creditMatch[1]);
391	    if (credit) copyright = credit;
392	  }
393	
394	  return {
395	    date: pageDate,
396	    title,
397	    explanation,
398	    url,
399	    hdurl,
400	    media_type: mediaType,
401	    copyright,
402	  };
403	}
404	
405	async function findLatestResolvable(
406	  log: string[], devFlags: DevFlags, apiKey: string,
407	): Promise<ResolvedApod> {
408	  let unresolvable = 0;
409	  let errors = 0;
410	
411	  for (let i = 0; i <= MAX_LOOKBACK_DAYS; i++) {
412	    const d = new Date();
413	    d.setDate(d.getDate() - i);
414	    const date = d.toLocaleDateString("en-CA", { timeZone: "America/New_York" });
415	
416	    try {
417	      const apod = await fetchApod(log, devFlags, apiKey, date);
418	      const resolved = resolveApod(apod);
419	      if (resolved) {
420	        if (i > 0 || resolved.source !== "image") {
421	          log.push(`  [findLatest] ${date} → ${resolved.source} (lookback=${i})`);
422	        }
423	        return resolved;
424	      }
425	      unresolvable++;
426	    } catch (err) {
427	      errors++;
428	      const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : "unknown";
429	      log.push(`  [findLatest] ${date} → error, skipping (${msg})`);
430	    }
431	  }
432	
433	  throw new Error(
434	    `No image found in last ${MAX_LOOKBACK_DAYS + 1} days (${unresolvable} unresolvable, ${errors} errors)`,
435	  );
436	}
437	
438	function validateImageUrl(url: string): void {
439	  const parsed = new URL(url);
440	  if (parsed.protocol !== "https:") {
441	    throw new Error(`Blocked image fetch: non-HTTPS scheme (${parsed.protocol})`);
442	  }
443	  if (!ALLOWED_IMAGE_HOSTS.some((suffix) => parsed.hostname.endsWith(suffix))) {
444	    throw new Error(`Blocked image fetch: unexpected host (${parsed.hostname})`);
445	  }
446	}
447	
448	async function fetchImageCached(log: string[], url: string): Promise<Response> {
449	  validateImageUrl(url);
450	
451	  const cache = caches.default;
452	  const cacheReq = new Request(`https://api.nasapicture.com/_cache/image/${encodeURIComponent(url)}`);
453	  const staleReq = new Request(`https://api.nasapicture.com/_cache/image/${encodeURIComponent(url)}:stale`);
454	
455	  const cached = await cache.match(cacheReq);
456	  if (cached) {
457	    log.push(`  [fetchImage] ${url.slice(0, 80)}… → cache HIT`);
458	    return cached;
459	  }
460	
461	  const res = await fetch(url);
462	
463	  log.push(`  [fetchImage] ${url.slice(0, 80)}… → ${res.status}`);
464	
465	  if (!res.ok) {
466	    // Try stale cache before giving up
467	    const stale = await cache.match(staleReq);
468	    if (stale) {
469	      log.push(`  [fetchImage] ${url.slice(0, 80)}… → stale cache fallback`);
470	      return stale;
471	    }
472	    throw new Error(`Image fetch failed: ${res.status}`);
473	  }
474	
475	  const contentType = res.headers.get("Content-Type") || "image/jpeg";
476	  const contentLength = res.headers.get("Content-Length");
477	  const cacheHeaders: Record<string, string> = {
478	    "Content-Type": contentType,
479	    "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${CACHE_TTL}`,
480	  };
481	  if (contentLength) cacheHeaders["Content-Length"] = contentLength;
482	
483	  const staleCacheHeaders = { ...cacheHeaders, "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${STALE_CACHE_TTL}` };
484	
485	  const arrayBuffer = await res.arrayBuffer();
486	  await Promise.all([
487	    cache.put(cacheReq, new Response(arrayBuffer, { headers: cacheHeaders })),
488	    cache.put(staleReq, new Response(arrayBuffer, { headers: staleCacheHeaders })),
489	  ]);
490	  return new Response(arrayBuffer, { headers: cacheHeaders });
491	}
492	
493	interface ImageDimensions {
494	  width: number;
495	  height: number;
496	}
497	
498	async function fetchImageDimensions(log: string[], imageUrl: string): Promise<ImageDimensions | null> {
499	  validateImageUrl(imageUrl);
500	
501	  const cache = caches.default;
502	  const cacheKey = `https://api.nasapicture.com/_cache/dimensions/${encodeURIComponent(imageUrl)}`;
503	  const cacheReq = new Request(cacheKey);
504	  const staleReq = new Request(`${cacheKey}:stale`);
505	
506	  const cached = await cache.match(cacheReq);
507	  if (cached) {
508	    log.push(`  [dimensions] ${imageUrl.slice(0, 80)}… → cache HIT`);
509	    return cached.json() as Promise<ImageDimensions>;
510	  }
511	
512	  try {
513	    const res = await fetch(imageUrl, {
514	      cf: { image: { format: "json" } },
515	    });
516	
517	    if (!res.ok) {
518	      const stale = await cache.match(staleReq);
519	      if (stale) {
520	        log.push(`  [dimensions] ${imageUrl.slice(0, 80)}… → stale cache fallback`);
521	        return stale.json() as Promise<ImageDimensions>;
522	      }
523	      log.push(`  [dimensions] ${imageUrl.slice(0, 80)}… → ${res.status} (failed)`);
524	      return null;
525	    }
526	
527	    const info = await res.json() as { original: { width: number; height: number } };
528	    const dimensions: ImageDimensions = {
529	      width: info.original.width,
530	      height: info.original.height,
531	    };
532	
533	    log.push(`  [dimensions] ${imageUrl.slice(0, 80)}… → ${dimensions.width}×${dimensions.height}`);
534	
535	    const body = JSON.stringify(dimensions);
536	    await Promise.all([
537	      cache.put(cacheReq, new Response(body, {
538	        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${CACHE_TTL}` },
539	      })),
540	      cache.put(staleReq, new Response(body, {
541	        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${STALE_CACHE_TTL}` },
542	      })),
543	    ]);
544	    return dimensions;
545	  } catch (err) {
546	    log.push(`  [dimensions] ${imageUrl.slice(0, 80)}… → error: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : "unknown"}`);
547	    const stale = await cache.match(staleReq);
548	    if (stale) return stale.json() as Promise<ImageDimensions>;
549	    return null;
550	  }
551	}
552	
553	function baseHeaders(origin: string, headers: Record<string, string> = {}): Record<string, string> {
554	  return {
555	    "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",
556	    "Cache-Control": `public, max-age=${CACHE_TTL}`,
557	    "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
558	    "Link": [
559	      `<${origin}/>; rel="alternate"; type="image/*"; title="HD image"`,
560	      `<${origin}/sd>; rel="alternate"; type="image/*"; title="SD image"`,
561	      `<${origin}/optimized>; rel="alternate"; type="image/*"; title="Optimized image"`,
562	      `<${origin}/thumb>; rel="alternate"; type="image/webp"; title="Thumbnail"`,
563	      `<${origin}/info>; rel="describedby"`,
564	      `<${origin}/about>; rel="about"`,
565	    ].join(", "),
566	    ...headers,
567	  };
568	}
569	
570	export default {
571	  async fetch(request: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {
572	    if (request.method === "OPTIONS") {
573	      return new Response(null, {
574	        headers: {
575	          "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",
576	          "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "GET, HEAD, OPTIONS",
577	          "Access-Control-Max-Age": "86400",
578	        },
579	      });
580	    }
581	
582	    if (request.method !== "GET" && request.method !== "HEAD") {
583	      return new Response(
584	        JSON.stringify({ error: "Method not allowed. This API only supports GET requests." }),
585	        { status: 405, headers: { "Allow": "GET, HEAD, OPTIONS", "Content-Type": "application/json" } },
586	      );
587	    }
588	
589	    const reqUrl = new URL(request.url);
590	    const { pathname } = reqUrl;
591	    const origin = reqUrl.origin;
592	    const start = Date.now();
593	
594	    const log: string[] = [];
595	    let res: Response;
596	
597	    try {
598	      const apiKey = env.NASA_API_KEY || "DEMO_KEY";
599	      const devFlags = parseDevFlags(reqUrl, env);
600	      if (devFlags.enabled && (devFlags.mode || devFlags.tools.size)) {
601	        log.push(
602	          `  [devFlags] mode=${devFlags.mode ?? "-"} tools=${
603	            devFlags.tools.size ? Array.from(devFlags.tools).join(",") : "-"
604	          }`,
605	        );
606	      }
607	
608	      const sdPaths = ["/sd", "/image-sd.jpg"];
609	      const hdPaths = ["/", "/image.jpg"];
610	      const optimizedPaths = ["/optimized", "/image-optimized.jpg"];
611	      const thumbPaths = ["/thumb", "/thumb.jpg"];
612	
613	      if (hdPaths.includes(pathname) || sdPaths.includes(pathname)) {
614	        const resolved = await findLatestResolvable(log, devFlags, apiKey);
615	        const imageUrl = sdPaths.includes(pathname)
616	          ? resolved.imageUrl
617	          : resolved.imageHdUrl;
618	
619	        const upstream = await fetchImageCached(log, imageUrl);
620	        const contentType = upstream.headers.get("Content-Type") || "image/jpeg";
621	
622	        res = new Response(upstream.body, {
623	          headers: baseHeaders(origin, { "Content-Type": contentType }),
624	        });
625	      } else if (optimizedPaths.includes(pathname)) {
626	        const resolved = await findLatestResolvable(log, devFlags, apiKey);
627	        const imageUrl = resolved.imageHdUrl;
628	        validateImageUrl(imageUrl);
629	
630	        const imageOpts: RequestInitCfPropertiesImage = {
631	          fit: "scale-down",
632	          width: 1200,
633	          quality: 85,
634	        };
635	
636	        const accept = request.headers.get("Accept") || "";
637	        if (/image\/avif/.test(accept)) {
638	          imageOpts.format = "avif";
639	        } else if (/image\/webp/.test(accept)) {
640	          imageOpts.format = "webp";
641	        }
642	
643	        log.push(`  [optimized] ${imageUrl.slice(0, 80)}… → cf.image ${JSON.stringify(imageOpts)}`);
644	
645	        const upstream = await fetch(imageUrl, {
646	          cf: { image: imageOpts },
647	        });
648	
649	        if (!upstream.ok) {
650	          throw new Error(`Image transform failed: ${upstream.status}`);
651	        }
652	
653	        const contentType = upstream.headers.get("Content-Type") || "image/jpeg";
654	
655	        res = new Response(upstream.body, {
656	          headers: baseHeaders(origin, { "Content-Type": contentType }),
657	        });
658	      } else if (thumbPaths.includes(pathname)) {
659	        const resolved = await findLatestResolvable(log, devFlags, apiKey);
660	        const imageUrl = resolved.imageHdUrl;
661	        validateImageUrl(imageUrl);
662	
663	        const imageOpts: RequestInitCfPropertiesImage = {
664	          fit: "scale-down",
665	          width: 32,
666	          quality: 30,
667	          format: "webp",
668	          blur: 5,
669	        };
670	
671	        log.push(`  [thumb] ${imageUrl.slice(0, 80)}… → cf.image ${JSON.stringify(imageOpts)}`);
672	
673	        const upstream = await fetch(imageUrl, {
674	          cf: { image: imageOpts },
675	        });
676	
677	        if (!upstream.ok) {
678	          throw new Error(`Thumbnail transform failed: ${upstream.status}`);
679	        }
680	
681	        const contentType = upstream.headers.get("Content-Type") || "image/webp";
682	
683	        res = new Response(upstream.body, {
684	          headers: baseHeaders(origin, { "Content-Type": contentType }),
685	        });
686	      } else if (pathname === "/info") {
687	        const endpoints = {
688	          "/": "Today's APOD image (high resolution, falls back to standard)",
689	          "/image.jpg": "Same as / with file extension (for contexts that need one)",
690	          "/sd": "Today's APOD image (standard resolution)",
691	          "/image-sd.jpg": "Same as /sd with file extension",
692	          "/optimized": "Optimized image (≤1200px, auto WebP/AVIF)",
693	          "/image-optimized.jpg": "Same as /optimized with file extension",
694	          "/thumb": "Tiny blurred thumbnail (32px WebP, ~1KB)",
695	          "/thumb.jpg": "Same as /thumb with file extension",
696	          "/info": "JSON metadata for today's APOD (includes image dimensions)",
697	          "/about": "Plain-text description and attribution",
698	        };
699	
700	        try {
701	          const resolved = await findLatestResolvable(log, devFlags, apiKey);
702	          const { apod, source, imageHdUrl } = resolved;
703	          const dimensions = await fetchImageDimensions(log, imageHdUrl);
704	
705	          res = new Response(
706	            JSON.stringify({
707	              title: apod.title,
708	              date: apod.date,
709	              explanation: apod.explanation,
710	              media_type: apod.media_type,
711	              url: apod.url,
712	              hdurl: apod.hdurl ?? null,
713	              copyright: apod.copyright ?? null,
714	              width: dimensions?.width ?? null,
715	              height: dimensions?.height ?? null,
716	              image_source: source,
717	              endpoints,
718	            }, null, 2),
719	            { headers: baseHeaders(origin, { "Content-Type": "application/json" }) },
720	          );
721	        } catch (err) {
722	          const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : "Unknown error";
723	          const status = err instanceof NasaApiError && err.statusCode === 429 ? 429 : 502;
724	          res = new Response(
725	            JSON.stringify({ error: message, endpoints }, null, 2),
726	            { status, headers: baseHeaders(origin, { "Content-Type": "application/json" }) },
727	          );
728	        }
729	      } else if (pathname === "/about") {
730	        const text = [
731	          "",
732	          "     .        *          .          *          .        *",
733	          "   .         *                        .          .",
734	          "                 _   _    _    ____    _",
735	          "     *          | \\ | |  / \\  / ___|  / \\         .",
736	          "        .       |  \\| | / _ \\ \\___ \\ / _ \\",
737	          "           .    | |\\  |/ ___ \\ ___) / ___ \\   *",
738	          "     .          |_| \\_/_/   \\_\\____/_/   \\_\\        .",
739	          "  *                              .                *",
740	          "        .    *        .    *          .        .",
741	          "",
742	          "                   ── APOD Proxy ──",

     1	# NASA Picture Proxy
     2	
     3	A Cloudflare Worker that proxies [NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD)](https://apod.nasa.gov/apod/astropix.html) behind a fixed URL. An HTTP GET request returns today's image without needing an API key or parsing JSON.
     4	
     5	[nasapicture.com](https://nasapicture.com) · [GitHub](https://github.com/GDKeller/nasa-picture-proxy)
     6	
     7	![Today's APOD](https://api.nasapicture.com/image-sd.jpg)
     8	*This is a static URL, but it'll be a different image when you visit this repo tomorrow.*
     9	
    10	During a tinkering session, I wanted to set the background image of my homelab [homepage](https://github.com/gethomepage/homepage) dashboard to the APOD. I didn't want to inject additional JavaScript on the page and couldn't find an existing static URL. So, I built this proxy to share with anyone else who'd like to view the wonders of space easily, anywhere.
    11	
    12	
    13	## Usage
    14	
    15	Embed directly as an image:
    16	
    17	```html
    18	<img src="https://api.nasapicture.com/" alt="NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day" />
    19	```
    20	
    21	CSS background:
    22	
    23	```css
    24	body {
    25	  background-image: url("https://api.nasapicture.com/");
    26	  background-size: cover;
    27	}
    28	```
    29	
    30	**Need a file extension?** Some contexts (RSS feeds, Open Graph tags, markdown renderers) require a URL that ends in an image extension. You can add `/image.jpg` or `/image-sd.jpg` as well:  
    31	```
    32	https://api.nasapicture.com/image.jpg
    33	https://api.nasapicture.com/image-sd.jpg
    34	```  
    35	
    36	Fetch metadata:
    37	
    38	```bash
    39	curl https://api.nasapicture.com/info | jq .
    40	```
    41	
    42	Returns data from the APOD API:
    43	- Direct URLs of APOD images
    44	- Date
    45	- Image title
    46	- Image explanation
    47	- Copyright info
    48	
    49	> [!TIP]
    50	> For those without the tech savvy to understand (i.e. remember) "api", all routes are also accessible at `get.nasapicture.com`
    51	
    52	## Endpoints
    53	
    54	| Path | Response |
    55	|------|----------|
    56	| `/` | Today's APOD image (HD, falls back to standard) |
    57	| `/image.jpg` | Same as `/` with file extension |
    58	| `/sd` | Standard resolution image |
    59	| `/image-sd.jpg` | Same as `/sd` with file extension |
    60	| `/optimized` | Optimized image (≤1200px, auto WebP/AVIF) |
    61	| `/image-optimized.jpg` | Same as `/optimized` with file extension |
    62	| `/thumb` | Tiny blurred thumbnail (32px WebP, ~1KB) |
    63	| `/thumb.jpg` | Same as `/thumb` with file extension |
    64	| `/info` | JSON metadata (title, date, explanation, copyright, image dimensions) |
    65	| `/about` | Plain-text description and route listing |
    66	
    67	When the APOD of the day is a video, the proxy serves NASA's video thumbnail. If there's no thumbnail, it walks backwards up to 7 days to find the most recent image.
    68	
    69	## How it works
    70	
    71	Both the NASA API call and the upstream image fetch are cached at Cloudflare's edge via `cf: { cacheTtl, cacheEverything }`. Caching is purely edge-based; there's no KV, D1, or cron involved.
    72	
    73	When the date rolls over, `formatDate(new Date())` produces a new date string, which changes the API request URL and therefore the cache key. The response updates automatically.
    74	
    75	## Author
    76	
    77	Built by [Grant Keller](https://grantkeller.dev).
     1	# CLAUDE.md
     2	
     3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
     4	
     5	## Project Overview
     6	
     7	APOD Proxy — a Cloudflare Worker that proxies NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day API behind stable, fixed URLs.
     8	
     9	## Commands
    10	
    11	- `npm run dev` starts the API (localhost:8787) and landing page (localhost:8788) in the background. Check them with `npm run status`, stop them with `npm run stop`, and read logs with the `npm run log:*` scripts.
    12	- Type-check with `npx tsc --noEmit`. There is no build artifact; Wrangler bundles `src/` directly.
    13	
    14	## Architecture
    15	
    16	Caching uses the Workers Cache API (`caches.default`) with a two-tier strategy — no KV, D1, or cron:
    17	- **Primary cache** (6h TTL): APOD metadata keyed by ET date, image bytes keyed by NASA URL
    18	- **Stale fallback** (24h TTL): same data under a `:stale` suffixed key, served when NASA's API is down or rate-limited
    19	
    20	Cache keys are date-based in `America/New_York` timezone, so they roll over at midnight ET. Cache key URLs must use a zone-scoped hostname (`https://api.nasapicture.com/_cache/...`), not synthetic hostnames -- `caches.default` silently drops writes for unknown hosts.
    21	
    22	The landing page (`landing/`) is served at `nasapicture.com` via Cloudflare Pages. The Worker serves `api.nasapicture.com` and `get.nasapicture.com`. Brand voice and design context live in `landing/CLAUDE.md`; read it before writing user-facing copy anywhere, including the Worker's `/about` text.
    23	
    24	## Environment
    25	
    26	- **`NASA_API_KEY`** — optional secret; falls back to `DEMO_KEY` (30 req/hr, sufficient behind cache). Set via `npx wrangler secret put NASA_API_KEY`.
    27	- Local secrets go in `.dev.vars` (gitignored).
    28

1	import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach, vi } from "vitest";

7	// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
8	// In-memory stand-ins for globals the Worker reaches for. Node gives us
9	// Request/Response/fetch/URL natively; we only need to fake `caches.default`
10	// and route outbound `fetch` calls. The tests call the default export's
11	// fetch handler directly — no wrangler, no miniflare, no real network.
12	// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
13	
14	interface CacheEntry {
15	  body: ArrayBuffer;
16	  headers: [string, string][];
17	}
18	
19	function createCache() {
20	  const store = new Map<string, CacheEntry>();
21	  const cache = {
22	    async match(req: Request | string): Promise<Response | undefined> {
23	      const url = typeof req === "string" ? req : req.url;
24	      const entry = store.get(url);
25	      if (!entry) return undefined;
26	      return new Response(entry.body.slice(0), { headers: entry.headers });
27	    },
28	    async put(req: Request | string, res: Response): Promise<void> {
29	      const url = typeof req === "string" ? req : req.url;
30	      const body = await res.arrayBuffer();
31	      const headers: [string, string][] = [];
32	      res.headers.forEach((value, key) => headers.push([key, value]));
33	      store.set(url, { body, headers });
34	    },
35	    async delete(req: Request | string): Promise<boolean> {
36	      const url = typeof req === "string" ? req : req.url;
37	      return store.delete(url);
38	    },
39	    // helpers for assertions
40	    _keys: () => Array.from(store.keys()),
41	    _size: () => store.size,
42	  };
43	  return cache;
44	}
45	
46	type CacheMock = ReturnType<typeof createCache>;

48	interface FetchCall {
49	  url: string;
50	  method: string;
51	}
52	
53	type RouteHandler = (req: Request) => Response | Promise<Response>;
54	
55	function createFetchMock() {
56	  const routes: Array<{ match: (url: string) => boolean; handler: RouteHandler }> = [];
57	  const calls: FetchCall[] = [];
58	
59	  const fn: typeof fetch = async (input, init) => {
60	    const req =
61	      input instanceof Request
62	        ? new Request(input, init)
63	        : new Request(typeof input === "string" ? input : String(input), init);
64	    calls.push({ url: req.url, method: req.method });
65	    for (const route of routes) {
66	      if (route.match(req.url)) return route.handler(req);
67	    }
68	    throw new Error(`fetch mock: no route for ${req.url}`);
69	  };
70	
71	  return Object.assign(fn, {
72	    calls,
73	    when(matcher: string | RegExp, handler: RouteHandler) {
74	      const match =
75	        typeof matcher === "string"
76	          ? (url: string) => url.includes(matcher)
77	          : (url: string) => matcher.test(url);
78	      routes.push({ match, handler });
79	    },

182	// Encode an HTML string as UTF-16 LE with a BOM, matching the weird encoding
183	// NASA silently serves for at least one APOD page (ap260408.html — "Earthset").
184	// The `Content-Type` header still claims charset=UTF-8, so the scraper cannot
185	// trust it and has to sniff the BOM. This helper lets us reproduce that exact
186	// quirk in a test.
187	function utf16leBomResponse(html: string, status = 200): Response {
188	  const bytes = new Uint8Array(2 + html.length * 2);
189	  bytes[0] = 0xff;
190	  bytes[1] = 0xfe;
191	  for (let i = 0; i < html.length; i++) {
192	    const code = html.charCodeAt(i);
193	    bytes[2 + i * 2] = code & 0xff;
194	    bytes[2 + i * 2 + 1] = (code >> 8) & 0xff;
195	  }
196	  return new Response(bytes, {
197	    status,
198	    // Mimic NASA: wrong charset header on purpose.
199	    headers: { "Content-Type": "text/html; charset=UTF-8" },
200	  });
201	}

Create a new item in the `board/` project management system. The system spec is bundled with the plugin at `/Users/grant/Documents/Projects/BoardPM/plugin/spec/board-system-spec.md`.

## Existing Board Items

Before creating, check if a similar item already exists. If a close match is found, ask the user if they still want to create a new one.

## Scope Assessment

When the user requests a **TASK**, evaluate whether it is actually EPIC-sized before creating it. Look for these signals:

- Multiple distinct steps or deliverables in the description
- Multiple action verbs joined by "and" (e.g., "add auth and set up roles and integrate SSO")
- Work that spans different code areas or concerns
- Sub-steps that could be completed and shipped independently

**Quick test:** "Could someone meaningfully complete and ship part of this while the rest remains undone?" If yes → likely an EPIC.

If EPIC signals are present, suggest an EPIC + sub-TASKs with a concrete breakdown. For example:

> "This looks like it has multiple independent deliverables. Want me to create an EPIC with separate TASKs for each piece instead?"

**This is a soft suggestion only.** If the user says "just make it a task," comply without pushback.

This assessment only applies to TASK creation — do not second-guess EPICs, NOTEs, or other types.

## Arguments

The user provides the type and title: `/board:board-add task <title>`, `/board:board-add epic <title>`, etc.

If no type is given, ask the user what type of item to create.

## Determine Next ID

Run the ID assignment script:

```bash
bash "/Users/grant/Documents/Projects/BoardPM/plugin/scripts/next-id.sh" <TYPE> ./board
```

This scans all directories (including `board/archive/` and `.doc-ids`) and returns the next available 4-digit zero-padded ID.

## Create the File

Use the correct directory, frontmatter, and naming convention:

| Type | Directory | Filename Example |
|------|-----------|-----------------|
| task | `board/tasks/` | `TASK-0014_add-batch-processing.md` |
| epic | `board/planning/` | `EPIC-0009_batch-mode.md` |
| adr | `board/planning/` | `ADR-0002_chose-webgpu-over-wasm.md` |
| note | `board/planning/` | `NOTE-0001_explore-wasm-option.md` |
| reference | `board/reference/` | `REFE-0007_webgpu-overview.md` |
| resource | `board/resources/` | `RESO-0001_webgpu-article.md` |

## Frontmatter Templates

Task:
```yaml
---
type: task
status: backlog
priority: 2
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

Epic:
```yaml
---
type: epic
status: planning
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

ADR:
```yaml
---
type: adr
status: active
context_date: YYYY-MM-DD
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

Note:
```yaml
---
type: note
status: inbox
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

Reference:
```yaml
---
type: reference
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

Resource (ask user for URL):
```yaml
---
type: resource
status: inbox
url: <url>
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

## Naming Rules

- Convert title to kebab-case for filename
- Task titles MUST be imperative mood (start with a verb). If the user gives a noun phrase, rewrite it (e.g., "batch processing" -> "Add batch processing support")
- Use today's date for `created`

## After Creation

Show the file path and ask if the user wants to add more detail to the body.


ARGUMENTS: task, priority 3, parent EPIC-0002: Strengthen landing page type hierarchy (impeccable flat-type-hierarchy finding on landing/index.html)

board/planning/EPIC-0003_infrastructure-and-devops.md:22:### TASK-0021: Automated daily cache warming via Cron Trigger [P1]
board/planning/EPIC-0003_infrastructure-and-devops.md:24:Add a `scheduled()` handler with a cron trigger to warm the edge cache after APOD rollover. Calls `findLatestImage`, `fetchImageCached`, and `fetchImageDimensions` to populate metadata and image bytes proactively. **Combined with TASK-0020, guarantees a fresh entry in stale cache so outages never exhaust our fallback.**
board/planning/EPIC-0003_infrastructure-and-devops.md:26:### TASK-0011: Add R2 storage layer for APOD image archiving
board/planning/EPIC-0003_infrastructure-and-devops.md:28:Insert R2 between edge cache and NASA as a persistent origin. Every image fetched from NASA gets stored in R2, building an automatic archive. Layered lookup becomes: Edge cache -> R2 -> NASA.
board/planning/EPIC-0003_infrastructure-and-devops.md:30:Key structure: `{date}/hd.{ext}`, `{date}/sd.{ext}`, `{date}/info.json`. Current-day images re-validated against NASA for same-day corrections; past dates served from R2 unconditionally.
board/planning/EPIC-0003_infrastructure-and-devops.md:32:R2 archiving also unblocks TASK-0031 Phase 2 (local timezone rollover, ahead-of-ET) and TASK-0035 (gallery/archive).
board/planning/EPIC-0003_infrastructure-and-devops.md:41:2. **TASK-0021** [P1] — Cron cache warming. Now that scrape is in place, cron warming guarantees stale cache never runs dry.
board/planning/EPIC-0003_infrastructure-and-devops.md:42:3. TASK-0011 — R2 storage layer. Larger effort, unblocks follow-on features (gallery, timezone Phase 2).
board/planning/EPIC-0003_infrastructure-and-devops.md:47:- EPIC-0002 TASK-0031 Phase 2 (local timezone, ahead-of-ET) is blocked by TASK-0011
board/planning/EPIC-0005_social-sharing-previews.md:19:Render a 1200x630 branded PNG once per day inside the Worker via Satori. Cached 24h keyed to date, regenerates at rollover. The OG HTML then points `og:image` at `/og` instead of `/sd`.
board/reference/REFE-0001_dev-feature-flag-convention.md:16:- **Tools** — set of independent helper overlays. **Any combination on at once. Additive.** Examples: `palette`, `grid`, `cache-inspector`, `fps`.
board/reference/REFE-0001_dev-feature-flag-convention.md:110:| `?dev=video` | TASK-0019 | Return a hard-coded video APOD fixture *with* `thumbnail_url` so the video-thumbnail branch of `resolveApod` can be exercised. Only short-circuits for today's date; walkback iterations still hit the normal path. Bypasses the APOD cache entirely so fixture runs never pollute real cached data. |
board/reference/REFE-0001_dev-feature-flag-convention.md:111:| `?dev=video-no-thumb` | TASK-0019 | Return a hard-coded video APOD fixture *without* `thumbnail_url`. `resolveApod` returns null for today, so the walkback path runs and pulls the next resolvable day. |
board/reference/REFE-0001_dev-feature-flag-convention.md:112:| `?dev=nasa-error` | TASK-0020 | Skip the upstream NASA API fetch and route straight to the stale-cache-then-scrape fallback path. Bypasses the primary cache so every request reliably exercises the fallback. Stale cache still wins over scrape when present — scrape is the last resort. |
board/planning/NOTE-0027_preserve-apod-filename-on-download.md:7:# Preserve original APOD filename on download
board/planning/NOTE-0027_preserve-apod-filename-on-download.md:9:When a user downloads an image from `api.nasapicture.com` (or `get.`), the browser saves it as `api.nasapicture.jpg`, derived from the hostname because the URL path has no meaningful filename. We should set `Content-Disposition` so downloads use the original NASA asset name (e.g. `NGC1234_hubble1200.jpg`), preserving provenance and making the filename searchable against apod.nasa.gov.
board/planning/NOTE-0027_preserve-apod-filename-on-download.md:22:https://apod.nasa.gov/apod/image/2604/NGC1234_hubble1200.jpg
board/planning/NOTE-0027_preserve-apod-filename-on-download.md:26:`resolved.imageHdUrl` / `resolved.imageUrl` in `src/index.ts` already hold this URL by the time we build the response, so extraction is a one-liner.
board/planning/NOTE-0027_preserve-apod-filename-on-download.md:32:- `/` and `/image.jpg` — serve `imageHdUrl`, extension matches source
board/planning/NOTE-0027_preserve-apod-filename-on-download.md:44:     const last = pathname.split("/").pop() || "apod.jpg";
board/planning/NOTE-0027_preserve-apod-filename-on-download.md:60:- Video thumbnails come from YouTube/Vimeo (`maxresdefault.jpg`, etc.) and won't have meaningful names. That's fine — any original filename is better than `api.nasapicture.jpg`.
board/planning/NOTE-0027_preserve-apod-filename-on-download.md:70:- `curl -I https://api.nasapicture.com/ | grep -i content-disposition` returns the original NASA filename.
board/planning/NOTE-0027_preserve-apod-filename-on-download.md:71:- Saving the image in a browser uses that filename, not `api.nasapicture.jpg`.
